---
name: repo-scout
description: Collect repository evidence into evidence.md during evidence_collection and followup_evidence. Use when a ticket's next_action.role is "scout" or when evidence is needed to continue a ticket. Cheap-model role; the business rules live in the protocol, not here.
---

# repo-scout

A thin operational procedure. All business rules live in the protocol under
`.ai/workflow/`; read those files before acting. Do not restate protocol rules here.

## Phase scope

`evidence_collection`, `followup_evidence` (see `.ai/workflow/ROLES.md`).

## Procedure

1. Read `.ai/work/<ticket-id>/state.yaml` first — it is authoritative. When
   entering without chat history, `ai-workflow resume <ticket-id>` prints the
   read-only continuation brief (PROTOCOL.md §"Portable continuation").
2. Confirm `next_action.role` is `scout`. If it is not, do not act; hand back.
3. Read the protocol files listed in PROTOCOL.md §"Entering a ticket" that
   apply — at minimum `.ai/workflow/PROTOCOL.md` (especially §"Scouting and
   auditing"), `.ai/workflow/ROLES.md`, and `.ai/workflow/ARTIFACTS.md`.
4. Read the source artifacts referenced by `source_artifacts` in state.yaml
   (spec, ticket, plan). Reference them by path; never copy their content.
5. Record your working session:
   `ai-workflow claim <ticket-id> --harness <H> --model <M>`.
6. Collect repository facts into `evidence.md` per the Scout Report contract in
   `.ai/workflow/ARTIFACTS.md` (worked examples:
   `.ai/workflow/examples/scout-bug.md`, `.ai/workflow/examples/scout-feature.md`).
   That contract owns the collection doctrine — sections, Decision Questions,
   the FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN finding syntax, the stopping reason, and what
   is forbidden in evidence.md. Follow it exactly; this skill does not restate it.
7. The scout writes evidence and handoff only (PROTOCOL.md §"Scouting and
   auditing"): the evidence verdict is the auditor's (`ai-workflow set-gate`)
   and phase transitions belong to the checkpoint-handoff (`ai-workflow
   advance`). Leave both to them.
8. Write `handoff.md` per the contract in `.ai/workflow/ARTIFACTS.md` before
   stopping.
9. Commit per PROTOCOL.md §"Commits and rollback", or report readiness for the
   next phase transition.

Do not record the evidence verdict; do not write `decision.md`; do not advance
the phase (`ai-workflow advance`). Those belong to other roles (see
`.ai/workflow/ROLES.md`).

1	# Protocol: Repo-native Cross-Harness Agent Workflow
2	
3	Canonical sources: the spec `docs/specs/agent-workflow-protocol.md` and ADRs 0001/0002 in the kit repo. This directory is the protocol as installed into a target repository.
4	
5	## 1. Goal
6	
7	Any coding agent that can read and write a Git repository (Codex, TRAE, ZCode, ...) can, on entering the repo, determine from a small set of fixed files:
8	
9	> what task -> which phase -> what evidence exists -> what the next role/action is
10	
11	without relying on chat history. The repository is the only persistent source of truth for workflow state.
12	
13	## 2. Core principles
14	
15	1. The Git repository is the only persistent source of truth for workflow state.
16	2. `.ai/workflow/` holds the protocol and templates; `.ai/work/<ticket-id>/` holds ticket-level state and artifacts.
17	3. `state.yaml` is the machine-readable authoritative workflow state — the first file any harness reads.
18	4. Skills, AGENTS.md managed blocks, and project rules are adapters pointing at this protocol; they never copy protocol content.
19	5. Never overwrite existing repo documentation; existing specs, tickets, and plans are integrated by reference.
20	6. All install and migration operations are idempotent, non-destructive, and rollback-capable.
21	
22	## 3. Entering a ticket
23	
24	1. Read `.ai/work/<ticket-id>/state.yaml`. It is authoritative; chat history is never authoritative.
25	2. Note `phase` and `status`. The intended next step is `next_action`.
26	3. Check `claim`. If another session holds the claim, read `handoff.md` before doing anything.
27	4. Confirm your role matches `next_action.role` (see ROLES.md). If not, do not act; hand back.
28	
29	## 4. Phases and statuses
30	
31	The phase machine is linear with one evidence loop:
32	
33	```
34	UNINITIALIZED -> REQUIREMENT -> EVIDENCE_COLLECTION -> EVIDENCE_AUDIT
35	  -> (evidence insufficient) -> FOLLOWUP_EVIDENCE -> EVIDENCE_AUDIT
36	  -> TECHNICAL_DECISION -> PLANNING -> IMPLEMENTATION -> REVIEW -> DONE
37	```
38	
39	In `state.yaml`, phases are lowercase: `requirement`, `evidence_collection`, `evidence_audit`, `followup_evidence`, `technical_decision`, `planning`, `implementation`, `review`, `done`.
40	
41	On a `workflow_version: 2` Ticket there is one additional edge: `review -> implementation`, the append-only repair path taken after a `changes_requested` Review. It is not available to v1 Tickets.
42	
43	New work ships on `workflow_version: 2`: a current install renders its template as v2, so greenfield `start` and `adopt` both begin on the v2 contracts. An existing `workflow_version: 1` Ticket (and an unupgraded v1 install) keeps the frozen v1 semantics until it is explicitly converted with `upgrade-ticket`.
44	
45	Lateral statuses are orthogonal to phase and are never merged into it: `active`, `blocked`, `escalation_required`, `paused`, `abandoned`.
46	
47	A phase changes only via the transitions above. Do not invent transitions.
48	
49	## 5. Claim semantics
50	
51	`claim: {harness, model, claimed_at}` records which session is working on the ticket. It is a soft claim — advisory, not a lock. Set it when you begin a working session. A conflicting session must read `handoff.md` before taking over.
52	
53	## 6. Reading and updating state.yaml
54	
55	- Read `state.yaml` before acting; save it after every state change.
56	- Stamp `updated_at` on every save.
57	- Write only the restricted YAML subset documented in STATE_SCHEMA.md.
58	- Unknown fields are silently ignored — never an error, never deleted.
59	- Reference existing specs, tickets, and plans by path in `source_artifacts`; never copy them into `.ai/`.
60	
61	## 7. Writing artifacts
62	
63	Artifact contracts are in ARTIFACTS.md. In brief: evidence.md is the Scout Report, collected by a scout; evidence-audit.md answers only sufficiency questions; decision.md is senior-only; progress.md logs at task granularity per its template (`.ai/workflow/templates/progress.md`: actual changes, verification/results, deviations, unresolved problems); handoff.md has fixed sections plus a Repository State block. Each artifact's writer is defined in ROLES.md.
64	
65	### Scouting and auditing
66	
67	A scout turns an engineering request into a bounded, traceable report:
68	
69	1. Capture the observation snapshot first: current HEAD as `observed_commit` and relevant dirty paths as `dirty_changes`.
70	2. Record Decision Questions (DQs) tied to the decisions they affect. If the ticket supplies none, draft them from the request. Ambiguity that requires an architectural choice is escalated, not answered.
71	3. Record findings as FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN with stable F-IDs, precise anchors (file/line/symbol, key/record, or command/result/exit), the verification method, and its scope or limits. Negative searches state their scope and exclusions. INFERENCE cites its basis.
72	4. Record unresolved DQ/F IDs in Unknowns with decision impact and the next collection step; a critical UNKNOWN does not block report readiness but cannot open the Evidence Gate.
73	5. Stop when questions are answered or remaining gaps and the need for a new decision or resource are explicit. Write the stopping reason in the report's Handoff. An exhausted budget produces a partial report, not a successful investigation.
74	6. The scout writes evidence and handoff only — never production changes, final decisions, or its own sufficiency verdict. Necessary temporary diagnostics are permitted; record their outcomes and residual changes.
75	
76	The evidence-auditor reads the report and answers the four sufficiency questions in evidence-audit.md, then records the gate. On a `workflow_version: 2` Ticket the recorded verdict is bound to the audited Evidence and its audit artifact: changing either after a sufficient verdict is recorded makes the gate stale, and `validate` and decisionward advances report the same blocker until the auditor re-audits and records the gate again. Report readiness and evidence sufficiency are distinct: a ready report with a critical UNKNOWN still leaves the Gate insufficient until the auditor decides otherwise.
77	
78	### Registered execution readiness (workflow_version 2)
79	
80	On a `workflow_version: 2` Ticket an executor may not enter `implementation` or complete a task unless the ticket is genuinely ready. Before the `planning -> implementation` transition and before every `complete-task`, the kit requires:
81	
82	- a registered Plan (`source_artifacts.plan.path` + `sha256`); a missing or unregistered Plan is rejected;
83	- Plan byte identity and task-contract (task-hash) identity — changing the Plan or one of its task sections after registration is drift and is rejected;
84	- coherent counters — non-negative integers only (booleans are never integers), `completed_tasks == [1..current_task]`, `current_task <= total_tasks`, and the registered total matching the task-hash count;
85	- a current sufficient evidence gate (the fresh gate binding); and
86	- an active ticket — `blocked`, `paused`, `abandoned`, or `escalation_required` Status may not execute.
87	
88	When the State marks the repo as adopted (`migration.adopted_existing_repo`), the `adoption_checkpoint` must carry all six confirmation booleans as true — `continuation_safe` included — before an executor proceeds; an adopted but unconfirmed ticket is rejected. `validate` reports the same problems as ERROR findings in `implementation`, `review`, and `done`. Version 1 Tickets are unaffected: every one of these conditions is v2-only. `complete-task` requires `implementation` and the current registered Plan on v2; its optional `--total` cannot override the registered count (a disagreeing value is rejected, not written), and on completion the explicit `next_action.task` is refreshed.
89	
90	### Review and completion (workflow_version 2)
91	
92	On a `workflow_version: 2` Ticket the Reviewer owns the Review in an independent context (senior default): it reads `decision.md` and the registered Plan, independently verifies the acceptance criteria against the actual change and the recorded verification results **inside a prepared isolated snapshot** (section 9, §"Reviewer verification isolation and publication"), authors `review.md` as its own candidate report under that snapshot's scratch area (see ARTIFACTS.md), and has the verdict published by the guarded `set-review`; it writes no live record and performs no live commit. The Review Metadata `reviewed_commit` is a literal hexadecimal Git object ID (full, or an unambiguous abbreviation of at least seven hex digits) resolving to an ancestor of HEAD; HEAD, branch and tag names are rejected even when they resolve, and `set-review` stores the full resolved commit ID once — for `pass` and `changes_requested` alike — so the verdict is bound to the immutable change that was actually reviewed. A mechanical checkpoint-handoff alone cannot supply the technical verdict, so in `review` the route is `reviewer`, not `checkpoint-handoff`.
93	
94	Completion is gated:
95	
96	- entering `review` requires a genuinely finished implementation — every registered task complete, the readiness conditions still satisfied, and the required artifacts (`evidence.md`, `evidence-audit.md`, `decision.md`, `handoff.md`) present;
97	- `review -> done` requires a CURRENT passing Review — `review.verdict == "pass"`, the bound Review artifact unchanged, the bound `plan_sha256` still matching the registered Plan, and no code drift since the recorded commit. A missing verdict, `changes_requested`, or a stale binding is rejected; `done` is never silently reopened.
98	
99	Both recorded verdicts are re-assessed against their immutable bindings by `validate`, `resume`, and the mutation guards — a `changes_requested` keeps its Review bytes, literal commit, registered Plan and code identity exactly like a `pass`. Canonical sources: the spec `docs/specs/agent-workflow-protocol.md` and ADRs 0001/0002 in the kit repo. This directory is the protocol as installed into a target repository.

## 1. Goal

Any coding agent that can read and write a Git repository (Codex, TRAE, ZCode, ...) can, on entering the repo, determine from a small set of fixed files:

> what task -> which phase -> what evidence exists -> what the next role/action is

without relying on chat history. The repository is the only persistent source of truth for workflow state.

## 2. Core principles

1. The Git repository is the only persistent source of truth for workflow state.
2. `.ai/workflow/` holds the protocol and templates; `.ai/work/<ticket-id>/` holds ticket-level state and artifacts.
3. `state.yaml` is the machine-readable authoritative workflow state — the first file any harness reads.
4. Skills, AGENTS.md managed blocks, and project rules are adapters pointing at this protocol; they never copy protocol content.
5. Never overwrite existing repo documentation; existing specs, tickets, and plans are integrated by reference.
6. All install and migration operations are idempotent, non-destructive, and rollback-capable.

## 3. Entering a ticket

1. Read `.ai/work/<ticket-id>/state.yaml`. It is authoritative; chat history is never authoritative.
2. Note `phase` and `status`. The intended next step is `next_action`.
3. Check `claim`. If another session holds the claim, read `handoff.md` before doing anything.
4. Confirm your role matches `next_action.role` (see ROLES.md). If not, do not act; hand back.

## 4. Phases and statuses

The phase machine is linear with one evidence loop:

```
UNINITIALIZED -> REQUIREMENT -> EVIDENCE_COLLECTION -> EVIDENCE_AUDIT
  -> (evidence insufficient) -> FOLLOWUP_EVIDENCE -> EVIDENCE_AUDIT
  -> TECHNICAL_DECISION -> PLANNING -> IMPLEMENTATION -> REVIEW -> DONE
```

In `state.yaml`, phases are lowercase: `requirement`, `evidence_collection`, `evidence_audit`, `followup_evidence`, `technical_decision`, `planning`, `implementation`, `review`, `done`.

On a `workflow_version: 2` Ticket there is one additional edge: `review -> implementation`, the append-only repair path taken after a `changes_requested` Review. It is not available to v1 Tickets.

New work ships on `workflow_version: 2`: a current install renders its template as v2, so greenfield `start` and `adopt` both begin on the v2 contracts. An existing `workflow_version: 1` Ticket (and an unupgraded v1 install) keeps the frozen v1 semantics until it is explicitly converted with `upgrade-ticket`.

Lateral statuses are orthogonal to phase and are never merged into it: `active`, `blocked`, `escalation_required`, `paused`, `abandoned`.

A phase changes only via the transitions above. Do not invent transitions.

## 5. Claim semantics

`claim: {harness, model, claimed_at}` records which session is working on the ticket. It is a soft claim — advisory, not a lock. Set it when you begin a working session. A conflicting session must read `handoff.md` before taking over.

## 6. Reading and updating state.yaml

- Read `state.yaml` before acting; save it after every state change.
- Stamp `updated_at` on every save.
- Write only the restricted YAML subset documented in STATE_SCHEMA.md.
- Unknown fields are silently ignored — never an error, never deleted.
- Reference existing specs, tickets, and plans by path in `source_artifacts`; never copy them into `.ai/`.

  refusal is the design: removing or ignoring the stray artifact and running
  `prepare-review` again is the route to a fresh context, and nothing forces a
  publication past the refusal.
- `run-review` is how a reviewer's command actually executes on the supported
  profile. It runs one verifier command under the enforced `linux-bwrap-v1`
  boundary — `/snapshot` and `/scratch` writable, no live path and no supervisor
  `meta/` mounted at all, a cleared environment, no network, no host sockets —
  captures stdout/stderr, records the command's own exit status plus the residual
  snapshot changes as a supervisor receipt, and exits with that status.
  `--kind baseline` runs are the independent acceptance runs; the first accepted
  baseline is pinned to the prepared snapshot identity, so a probe edit can never
  promote itself into the baseline. `--kind probe` records the declared
  snapshot-relative edits, which stay in the receipt whether or not the reviewer
  restores them. A boundary blocker exits 1 and never falls back to an
  unconstrained run; an unsupported host reports a named blocker instead of
  support. The two host runbooks live in the **ai-workflow source repository**,
  not in an installed target: `adapters/local-review.md` records the host
  actually demonstrated (a Windows coordinator driving `bwrap` through WSL) and
  `adapters/codex/windows.md` records why no **Windows-native boundary** is: no
  Windows or Codex session's own tool-write restriction has been demonstrated on
  the host and build in use. That is a claim about the session's restriction, not
  about the boundary's availability, which the same Windows coordinator
  demonstrates through WSL. Nothing in this procedure depends on opening those
  files from a target repository: the runtime answer for any host is the prepared
  context's own `meta/preflight.json`, which either records an enforced boundary
  or fails closed with a named blocker and no receipt.
- Guarded `set-review` publishes, it does not judge: `--review-context`,
  `--report` and `--handoff` are required together, the report and handoff are
  the reviewer's own candidate bytes written under that context's `scratch/`, and
  the command re-reads the live code, Plan and inputs against the prepared
  manifest before writing. It writes only this Ticket's Review, State and Handoff
  through one journal-guarded transaction; a refusal changes no live record and no
  phase, and every hash pointer it publishes is the reviewer's exact bytes.

Two limits of the published mechanism stay stated rather than implied away:

- A publication consumes its context. `state.yaml` and `handoff.md` are captured
  inputs, so the currentness check refuses a second publication from one prepared
  context: each verdict needs a fresh `prepare-review` run and a fresh
  independent review of anything that changed.
- Journal recovery is deliberately conservative. When an interrupted transaction
  cannot hand its own bytes back, the context stays blocked and there is no
  operator-facing command to clear it; discarding that context and preparing a
  fresh snapshot is the only route, and nothing about that refusal publishes a
  verdict.

The reviewer therefore writes nothing live and performs no live commit.
Publication writes Review, State and Handoff through the public command; the
phase-boundary commit in §"Commits and rollback" belongs to checkpoint-handoff
afterwards, never to the reviewer.

### Portable continuation

A receiver resumes from persisted state and artifacts, never from chat history:

```
ai-workflow resume <ticket-id>
```

prints a read-only brief with the Ticket, State (phase/status/gate/escalation),
the next role/action/task, the repository branch/HEAD/dirty paths, the referenced
artifacts and their digests, and the continuation checks. It exits `0` for a valid
brief, `1` when the brief carries ERROR blockers or `state.yaml` cannot be read,
and `2` for a usage error; a readable blocked Ticket still prints the brief
(exit `1`). The command never writes `updated_at`, never claims the ticket, and
never mutates a file — it points at reports rather than copying them.

An Evidence report whose `observed_commit` is older than HEAD prompts a relevance
assessment of its anchors; those facts are not automatically discarded. Review
freshness follows the review checks in section 7. Version 1 Tickets print
explicit notices for the newer contracts instead of an invented gate or a
migration claim. Model tiers are Harness-local defaults (see ROLES.md); manual
model/Harness switching is supported and no automatic dispatch is assumed.

## 10. Commits and rollback

- Commit at every phase boundary; during implementation, commit per task.
- Every work commit uses the prefix `ai-workflow(<ticket-id>): <action>`, e.g. `ai-workflow(TICKET-017): task 4 complete`. Grepping `ai-workflow(` recovers the whole work history.
- The phase-boundary commit is both the handoff anchor and the rollback point.
- Recovery from a botched phase: `git revert` to the last phase-boundary commit, then record an `incident` block in `state.yaml` explaining what went wrong and how it was recovered.
- `abandoned` tickets stay on disk and can be resurrected by a senior role: roll back to the last boundary commit, record an incident block, re-claim.

## 11. Legacy adoption

For repos adopted from existing state (existing specs, tickets, plans, half-done work), follow MIGRATION.md: discovery -> migration report -> phase reconstruction -> retroactive minimum evidence -> decision reconstruction -> adoption checkpoint. Never fabricate artifacts for phases that were never executed.

### Explicit version conversion (`ai-workflow upgrade-ticket`)

`ai-workflow upgrade` upgrades only the installed protocol; it never rewrites a Ticket's `state.yaml` and never promotes its `workflow_version` in place. Converting a Ticket is explicit: `upgrade-ticket <ticket-id>` converts one interpretable active v1 Ticket to `workflow_version: 2` once, keeping its phase and history, resetting the gate to `insufficient` and the review to `pending`, and recording `upgrade.requires_reconstruction` together with an unresolved machine escalation whose resolver is `workflow-bootstrap` (preserving the interrupted `next_action`). It fabricates no audit, Plan or review pass, and a historical `done` Ticket stays v1. The converted Ticket is not valid until a senior resolver reconstructs the retained phase's current contracts through the public commands and clears the flag with `escalate --clear --resolution`. See MIGRATION.md and STATE_SCHEMA.md.

1	# Artifact Contracts
2	
3	All artifacts live under `.ai/work/<ticket-id>/`. Each has one writer role, an allowed content set, and a forbidden content set.
4	
5	| Artifact | Writer | Content | Forbidden |
6	|---|---|---|---|
7	| evidence.md | scout | Scout Report: Metadata, Decision Questions, Findings, Unknowns, Handoff; FACT / INFERENCE / UNKNOWN entries; important FACTs carry anchors | design proposals, the evidence verdict |
8	| evidence-audit.md | evidence-auditor | sufficiency answers only | recommendations, designs |
9	| decision.md | technical-decision (senior-only) | chosen approach, rejected alternatives, invariants, compatibility, API/schema decisions, risks, escalation boundaries | undecided design questions |
10	| plan.md | executor-plan (senior-only) | ordered bounded tasks, each with objective, Fact/decision inputs, allowed and protected scope, invariants, acceptance criteria, verification, dependencies, escalation conditions | an executor-selected or redesigned task |
11	| review.md | reviewer (senior default, independent context) | reviewed commit, registered Plan identity, acceptance results, verification commands/results, findings, verdict, required rework | a verdict for another commit or an unregistered Plan |
12	| progress.md | ticket-executor | task-granularity log: completed task, files changed, tests run, deviation, open issues | every shell command |
13	| handoff.md | checkpoint-handoff (or the departing agent) | fixed sections + Repository State block | unverified claims |
14	
15	## evidence.md (Scout Report, format_version=1)
16	
17	The Evidence artifact is the Scout Report. It is the only artifact a scout
18	writes. Design proposals and the evidence verdict (sufficient / insufficient)
19	are forbidden — the verdict belongs to the evidence-auditor via `set-gate`.
20	
21	Adopted repos carry a Migration Notice (see MIGRATION.md). Collection rounds
22	are retained: prior rounds, DQ/F IDs and collection history stay addressable.
23	
24	### Metadata
25	
26	Metadata lives in the first fenced yaml block under an exact H2 Metadata
27	heading; only that block goes through the restricted parser. All other content
28	is Markdown — never send commands, generic types, or arbitrary prose through
29	that parser.
30	
31	Required Metadata fields:
32	
33	- `artifact_type: evidence`
34	- `format_version: 1`
35	- `ticket_id`
36	- `round` — the positive current collection round (an integer; boolean,
37	  string, zero, and negative values are rejected); must match Audit/CLI round
38	- `observed_commit` — the repository HEAD at collection time as a literal
39	  hexadecimal object ID: a seven-hex-digit abbreviation up to the full object
40	  ID (never `HEAD`, a branch name, or a `<placeholder>`)
41	- `dirty_changes` — string list of relevant working-tree paths, or `[]`
42	- `created_at` — an ISO-8601 timestamp (a bare date or a full timestamp)
43	- `scout_harness`, `scout_model` — concrete Scout provenance, not placeholders
44	
45	`task_type` and `report_status` are optional descriptive fields, not State
46	enums. Capture `observed_commit` and `dirty_changes` at collection time and
47	keep the observed snapshot interpretable.
48	
49	### Required sections
50	
51	Required H2 sections, in order: Metadata, Decision Questions, Findings,
52	Unknowns, Handoff. Optional H2 sections (task-specific, conditional — no fixed
53	quota): Reproduction, Execution Path, Failure Boundary, Contracts, Constraints,
54	Change Surface. Bug investigations record reproduction and failure-boundary
55	outcomes, with reasons when they could not be established.
56	
57	### Decision Questions
58	
59	Three to eight questions is guidance, not a quota. If the ticket supplies no
60	questions, the scout drafts them from the request and may add factual
61	follow-ups. Ambiguity requiring an architectural choice is escalated, not
62	answered. Each question uses H3 `DQ-01` (two or more digits) with named fields:
63	
64	- **Question:** the question as investigated
65	- **Decision affected:** which decision this question feeds
66	- **Evidence targets:** likely files, areas, or behaviors worth collecting
67	- **Answer:** `ANSWERED` | `UNKNOWN`
68	- **Facts:** linked F-IDs, or an explicit UNKNOWN fact-link value when unresolved
69	
70	### Findings
71	
72	Each finding uses H3 `F-01 [FACT | INFERENCE | UNKNOWN]` with named fields:
73	
74	- **Statement:** one precise claim
75	- **Questions:** associated DQ IDs — every finding cites at least one
76	  established question
77	- **Sources:** anchored source list (see below)
78	- **Method:** `static` | `execution` | `test` | `inference` | `unknown`
79	- **Scope:** limits of the claim
80	- **Basis:** required for INFERENCE and must cite at least one established
81	  F-ID; optional otherwise
82	
83	Named fields use `**Label:** value`; multiline lists continue below the label.
84	Recognise fields outside code fences only. FACT means an observed claim, not a
85	confidence score; optional confidence grades cannot replace evidence. Static
86	reading, execution, and test verification are distinct methods — do not present
87	static reading as runtime verification.
88	
89	Sources use a supported family prefix — `code:`, `config:`, `data:`,
90	`runtime:`, `negative search:`, `inference basis:`, `unknown:` — and any other
91	entry is rejected as non-concrete:
92	
93	- code/config/data anchors: `code: src/example.py:10-14 :: Example.method` — a
94	  repository-relative path, a `:12` line or `:12-18` range (line numbers start
95	  at 1; a range may not be zero or reversed), and a `::` anchor naming the
96	  symbol, key, or record. A file without a named symbol uses a justified
97	  `:: file scope (reason: ...)` anchor rather than a fabricated function name.
98	- runtime anchors: `runtime: <command> / input: <input or fixture> /
99	  result: <observed result> / exit: <integer exit status>` — command, input,
100	  observed result, and integer exit status are required; the labels
101	  `observed result:` and `exit status:` are accepted aliases of `result:` and
102	  `exit:`.
103	- negative searches: `negative search: scope <where searched> /
104	  exclusions: <excluded areas or none> / result: <outcome>` — scope,
105	  exclusions, and result are required; a search never needs a fabricated file.
106	- inference basis: `inference basis: F-01, F-02` — at least one cited F-ID.
107	- unknown: `unknown: <unobserved item> / collect at: <collection target>` —
108	  the unobserved item and the collection target are required; allowed only on
109	  an `F-NN [UNKNOWN]` finding.
110	
111	These source checks are shapes only: no file existence is verified and no
112	claim is judged — sufficiency and truth remain the auditor's role.
113	
114	### Unknowns
115	
116	The Unknowns section names the unresolved DQ/F IDs, the decision impact of each,
117	and the next collection step; explicit `None` is valid. A critical UNKNOWN does
118	not block report readiness, but it cannot open the Evidence Gate — only the
119	auditor judges sufficiency.
120	
121	### Handoff
122	
123	The Handoff section lists established Fact IDs, decisions still required,
124	precise missing evidence, areas already investigated, and the stopping reason.
125	Report readiness and evidence sufficiency are distinct: a report with a
126	critical UNKNOWN can be ready for audit while the Gate remains insufficient.
127	
128	## evidence-audit.md
129	
130	Metadata lives in the first fenced yaml block under an exact H2 Metadata
131	heading, with required fields: `artifact_type: evidence-audit`,
132	`format_version: 1`, `ticket_id`, `round`, `gate`, `evidence_sha256`. The
133	`evidence_sha256` field is the SHA-256 of the audited Evidence report; it is
134	computed when the gate is recorded and IS written into the audit artifact's
135	Metadata. The audit artifact's own SHA-256 is never computed and inserted
136	into itself.
137	
138	After Metadata, keep exactly the existing four sufficiency-question H2s; each
139	has a substantive answer or a justified not-applicable:
140	
141	1. Is the evidence sufficient to enter technical_decision?
142	2. What is missing?
143	3. Why might the gap change a decision?
144	4. What should the next scout collect precisely?
145	
146	Assess DQ coverage, traceability, verification limits, and decision-changing
147	unknowns within those questions. Answers only sufficiency — no recommendations,
148	no designs.
149	
150	## decision.md
151	
152	Written only by a senior model (technical-decision role). Contains:
153	
154	- Chosen approach
155	- Rejected alternatives
156	- Invariants
157	- Compatibility
158	- API / schema decisions
159	- Risks
160	- Escalation boundaries
161	
162	Adopted repos add a Provenance section recording only the still-valid API/schema/invariants/architecture (see MIGRATION.md).
163	
164	## plan.md (format_version=1)
165	
166	The Plan is the referenced execution contract, written by the senior
167	`executor-plan` role and integrated by reference (`source_artifacts.plan`) — never
168	copied into `.ai/`. It decomposes the decision into ordered, bounded tasks.
169	
170	Metadata lives in the first fenced yaml block under an exact H2 Metadata
171	heading, with required fields: `artifact_type: plan`, `format_version: 1`,
172	`ticket_id`, `task_count` (the number of ordered `Task N` sections).
173	
174	After Metadata, use ordered H2 `Task 1`, `Task 2`, … Each task carries named H3
175	sections, in order:
176	
177	- **Objective** — one bounded step an executor can complete without inventing design
178	- **Inputs** — referenced Fact IDs and the decision from `decision.md`
179	- **Allowed changes** — the files or areas the executor may modify
180	- **Protected scope** — behavior, interfaces, or data that must not change
181	- **Invariants** — properties that must still hold
182	- **Acceptance criteria** — observable conditions that make the task complete
183	- **Verification** — exact commands and expected outcomes
184	- **Dependencies** — earlier task numbers, or a justified `N/A`
185	- **Escalation conditions** — what forces a senior decision instead of improvisation
186	
187	Dependency numbers must reference earlier tasks only; a forward or self
188	dependency is invalid. A justified `N/A` (or `none`) is valid; a bare empty
189	placeholder is not. Open architecture decisions prevent handing a task to an
190	executor.
191	
192	On a `workflow_version: 2` Ticket, `register-plan <ticket-id> --path <plan>
193	--total N` reads and validates the Plan, bounds its path to the repository,
194	checks the declared count, and records `source_artifacts.plan.path` and
195	`source_artifacts.plan.sha256` (the raw-byte hash) plus the ordered
196	`implementation.task_hashes`. Registration is allowed only in `planning`, a
197	recorded senior escalation resolution, or a strictly-appending
198	`changes_requested` review; a rejected registration changes no State bytes.
199	
200	## review.md (format_version=1)
201	
202	The Review is the Reviewer's structural verdict on the current change and
203	registered Plan. The Reviewer owns technical conformance in an independent
204	context (senior default); mechanical checkpoint-handoff alone cannot supply it.
205	
206	### Metadata
207	
208	Metadata lives in the first fenced yaml block under an exact H2 Metadata
209	heading, with required fields: `artifact_type: review`, `format_version: 1`,
210	`ticket_id`, `reviewed_commit`, `plan_sha256`, and `verdict`
211	(`pass` | `changes_requested`).
212	
213	`reviewed_commit` must be a literal hexadecimal Git object ID: the
214	repository's full object ID, or an unambiguous abbreviation of at least seven
215	hex digits, resolving to a commit that is an ancestor of the current HEAD.
216	HEAD, branch and tag names are rejected even when they resolve — a recorded
217	review must never follow a moving ref — and a ref named like a hexadecimal
218	prefix never takes precedence over the object carrying it.
219	
220	### Required sections
221	
222	Required H2 sections, in order, after Metadata: `Acceptance results`,
223	`Verification results`, `Findings`, `Required rework`. `Acceptance results` and
224	`Verification results` must be substantive for BOTH verdicts; `Findings` and
225	`Required rework` may be the explicit text `None` for a `pass` and must be
226	substantive for a `changes_requested`. Extra nonreserved prose sections are
227	allowed.
228	
229	### Verification provenance for new isolated reviews
230	
231	One H2 heading is reserved: `## Isolation provenance`, recorded under
232	`Verification results` as exactly one fenced `json` block. Its required keys are
233	`format_version`, `reviewed_commit`, `context_sha256`, `live_manifest_sha256`,
234	`snapshot_manifest_sha256`, `plan_sha256`, `input_hashes`, `boundary`, `runs`,
235	`probe_changes`, `residual_changes` and `limits`; `runs` entries carry
236	`run_id`, `kind`, `argv`, `exit_code`, `stdout_sha256`, `stderr_sha256`,
237	`snapshot_before` and `snapshot_after`, and the list has to distinguish the two
238	kinds — at least one `baseline` acceptance run and at least one `probe` run —
239	because a guarded publication refuses a report whose cited runs name only one
240	kind, and every receipt recorded under `meta/runs/` must be cited; `boundary`
241	carries `profile`, `enforced`,
242	`preflight` and `preflight_sha256`; each `probe_changes` entry carries `path`,
243	`before_sha256`, `after_sha256` and `deleted`, and `deleted` is true exactly when
244	`after_sha256` is null — an edited or added path pairs `deleted: false` with its
245	`after_sha256`, and only a deletion may carry null; `residual_changes` carries
246	`modified`, `added` and `removed`. Every value the supervisor's records carry is
247	read from them, never retyped: `prepare-review` writes `meta/context.json` with
248	the live and snapshot manifests, `run-review` writes `meta/preflight.json` and one
249	receipt per verifier command, and the published Report must equal the reviewer's
250	candidate bytes exactly. A Report that carries
251	this section can only be recorded through the guarded
252	`set-review <ticket-id> --verdict <pass|changes_requested> --review-context <dir>
253	--report <candidate-review.md> --handoff <candidate-handoff.md>`; the ordinary
254	unguarded form refuses it, and a legacy Report without the section keeps its
255	historical behavior.
256	
257	Under `Verification results`, a new isolated review records:
258	
259	- The full reviewed commit and separate live/snapshot baseline content identities
260	  (path/content manifests or immutable referenced manifests), the registered
261	  Plan's raw-byte hash and the raw identities of relevant verification inputs.
262	- The snapshot location, permitted output scope, actual Harness/host restriction
263	  and the controlled disposable-sentinel denial result. Do not copy private
264	  machine paths or global settings into shared project files; use a portable
265	  snapshot identifier and repository-relative evidence references.
266	- Actual commands, execution directory/scope, exit status and observed results,
267	  including failures and unavailable checks. Static reading is not a test run.
268	- Every temporary probe's affected paths and behavior, baseline versus modified
269	  test runs, residual snapshot changes, limitations and what each result proves.
270	  Restoring probe bytes is not grounds to omit the execution record.
271	- The guarded publication step's currentness check and any mismatch/blocker.
272	  Only a successful check permits publication of the reviewer's verdict.
273	
274	Keep Review Metadata and existing raw-byte bindings unchanged. These provenance
275	requirements apply to newly produced isolated reviews; old artifacts retain
276	historical validity and are not retroactively presented as isolation evidence.
277	Structural report checks cannot attest that a host denied writes or that a
278	narrative is true. The launch boundary needs actual denial evidence, and that
279	evidence is now produced by the commands above rather than promised:
280	`run-review` records the sentinel denials, the writable scopes, the absence of
281	any live or `meta/` mount, the cleared environment and the network refusal, and
282	publication refuses a provenance claim that disagrees with the persisted receipt
283	in every field the supervisor actually records — each cited run's `kind`,
284	`argv`, `exit_code`, `stdout_sha256`, `stderr_sha256`, `snapshot_before` and
285	`snapshot_after` plus its recorded `profile`, the captured context, manifest and
286	input identities, and the persisted boundary evidence — together with the rule
287	that no recorded receipt may go uncited. Fields the receipts cannot corroborate
288	stay reviewer-authored claims, and publication checks their shape, never their
289	truth: the `limits` list, the inner commands a run's `argv` goes on to invoke,
290	and a probe's `before_sha256`/`after_sha256` (a receipt names the observed paths,
291	not per-path content hashes). That is precisely why those claims stay visible in
292	the record. What that still does not buy is stated plainly: a host without an
293	available boundary gets a named blocker and no publishable isolation provenance
294	(the two host runbooks, `adapters/local-review.md` and
295	`adapters/codex/windows.md`, live in the ai-workflow source repository rather
296	than in an installed target; the runtime answer for the host you are actually on
297	is the prepared context's own `meta/preflight.json`, which fails closed with that
298	named blocker), and matching
299	receipts prove the recorded runs happened under the recorded mounts — they do
300	not prove the review's technical judgment or its acceptance conclusion.
301	
302	Recording the verdict with `set-review <ticket-id> --verdict pass|changes_requested`
303	binds it to the Review artifact's raw-byte SHA-256, the full resolved commit ID
304	(stored once in State, for both verdicts), and the registered Plan SHA-256 (see
305	`STATE_SCHEMA.md`). A missing or placeholder artifact, a Metadata `verdict` that
306	disagrees with the CLI, a `plan_sha256` that disagrees with the registered Plan,
307	a `reviewed_commit` that is symbolic, ambiguous, a non-commit, or an unrelated
308	history, or any change to the reviewed code, tests, fixtures, or Plan since the
309	reviewed commit rejects the command and leaves State unchanged. Only this
310	Ticket's own `state.yaml`, `progress.md`, `handoff.md`, and `review.md` are
311	exempt from the code-drift check. Structural validity is not proof that
312	acceptance criteria passed.
313	
314	Hint neutralization happens only inside a disposable index copy and changes no
315	binding: `validate`, `resume`, the `review -> done` gate and `archive-artifacts`
316	all re-assess through that same rule, so an `assume-unchanged` or
317	`skip-worktree` hint cannot leave a recorded verdict current for one consumer
318	while another sees the change, and a relevant path absent because sparse checkout
319	excluded it is drift or a named blocker rather than silence. A refused
320	`archive-artifacts` writes nothing at all: the binding is checked before any
321	file is created, so neither the requested path nor the temporary file the writer
322	would stage beside it appears in the output directory.
323	
324	Both recorded verdicts are re-assessed against their immutable bindings by
325	`validate`, `resume`, and the mutation guards: a `pass` and a
326	`changes_requested` each keep matching Review bytes, the same literal commit,
327	the registered Plan, and unchanged reviewed code. A previously stored symbolic
328	binding (for example `reviewed_commit: HEAD` or a branch name from an older
329	State) is stale: it is reported and requires a new independent review — today's
330	HEAD is never resolved as the old approval. A `pass` completes the ticket only
331	while it is current: `review -> done` is rejected once the Review artifact, the
332	registered Plan, or the reviewed code changes. A `changes_requested` is repaired
333	append-only — the senior registers an appending rework Plan (`register-plan`)
334	and `review -> implementation` clears the failed verdict to `pending`,
335	preserving the completed prefix and routing to the first appended task. The
336	recorded Review must be unchanged for that repair; a stale failed Review is
337	re-recorded, not reused. The re-registration itself may replace the failed
338	Review's Plan identity, and only that Plan drift is excused — never source-code
339	drift or changed Review bytes — and only while the completed task contracts are
340	unchanged. A recorded `pass` never inherits that exception.
341	
342	## progress.md
343	
344	Execution log at task granularity: completed task, files changed, tests run, deviation from plan, open issues. Not every shell command.
345	
346	## handoff.md
347	
348	Fixed sections, in order: What was done / What remains / Important discoveries / Artifact identity / Verification limits / Known relevant drift / Current failure (if any; the shorter heading `Current failure` is accepted as its alias) / Do not repeat / Next recommended action. Plus a Repository State block with the four fields Branch, HEAD, Uncommitted files, and Test status.
349	
350	### Handoff readiness (workflow_version 2)
351	
352	`contracts.validate_handoff` checks the readiness syntax of a handoff — shapes only, never narrative truth:
353	
354	- every required section present, and prose sections substantive (not empty, not one whole-value template token; multiline template blocks are detected too);
355	- `Artifact identity` and `Known relevant drift` keep structured bullets, and every bullet's label value is concrete — the Evidence/Audit/Decision/Plan/Review identities and the drift bullets may not carry whole-value template tokens or standalone `<placeholder>` words;
356	- `Repository State` carries concrete Branch/HEAD/Uncommitted files/Test status values.
357	
358	Comparisons and code literals that merely contain angle brackets (generics, inline code, `a < b`) are not placeholders. Explicit `None` and a justified `N/A — reason` are legitimate where no item exists.
359	
360	Readiness is a **transfer boundary, not proof of acceptance**. Early drafts stay permitted: outside the boundaries the same problems are WARN notices. The gates are entering `review` (implementation -> review), completing to `done`, continuing in `review`/`done` (validate and resume through the shared phase checks), and clearing an implementation/review recovery — a rejected gate leaves State unchanged. A ready handoff never verifies that the narrative is true and never implies the acceptance criteria passed.
361	
362	## v2 structural validation (workflow_version 2)
363	
364	The grammar above is enforced structurally for Version 2 Tickets; Version 1
365	Tickets keep their existing semantics. Structural validation checks shapes, not
366	truth: it never proves a claim or judges a design.
367	
368	Reading rules:
369	
370	- Only H2/H3 headings **outside code fences** become sections/records; a fenced
371	  fake heading is never a boundary.
372	- Metadata is the **first** fenced yaml block under the exact H2 `Metadata`;
373	  only that block goes through the restricted parser. Duplicate Metadata keys
374	  and duplicate DQ/F IDs are errors, as are constructs outside the restricted
375	  YAML subset (ADR-0002).
376	
377	Reported structural problems include:
378	
379	- missing required Metadata fields or required H2 sections, sections out of order
380	- illegal IDs (DQ-NN / F-NN), missing or illegal finding tag, illegal
381	  `Method`/`Answer` values
382	- empty values or bare `<placeholder>` stand-ins in required fields
383	- a Metadata `round` that is not a positive integer (boolean, string, zero, and
384	  negative rounds rejected; the Evidence, Audit, and CLI rounds must agree), an
385	  `observed_commit` that is not a literal 7–64 hex-digit object ID, a
386	  non-ISO-8601 `created_at`, a non-string-list `dirty_changes`, or placeholder
387	  `scout_harness`/`scout_model`
388	- dangling references: `Facts`/`Basis` naming an unknown F-ID, `Questions`
389	  naming an unknown DQ-ID (an explicit `UNKNOWN` fact-link stays valid)
390	- an ANSWERED question citing no existing F-ID, a finding citing no existing
391	  DQ-ID, or an INFERENCE whose `Basis` cites no existing F-ID
392	- a Sources entry that is not a supported concrete family (a line-only or
393	  symbol-only code anchor, an unlabeled `trust me` entry, a runtime source
394	  without command/input/result/integer exit, a negative search without
395	  scope/exclusions/result, an `inference basis` without F-IDs, or an
396	  `unknown:` source off an [UNKNOWN] finding or without an unobserved item and
397	  collection target)
398	- a Metadata `ticket_id` that does not match the Ticket
399	
400	The Audit keeps exactly the four sufficiency-question H2s; its Metadata
401	`round` (a positive integer) and `gate` must match the State and CLI values,
402	and `evidence_sha256` must be a SHA-256 digest.
403	
404	The Plan (see above) is validated as ordered `Task N` sections with the nine
405	required H3 fields; contiguous task numbers, no forward/self dependency, and a
406	`task_count` agreeing with the sections are required. Its per-task identity is
407	the **canonical task hash**: SHA-256 of the task's section with CRLF changed to
408	LF and trailing whitespace removed, so line-ending conversion alone does not
409	rewrite registered history.
410	
411	Pending scaffold reports are only WARNed in `requirement`/`evidence_collection`
412	and are never treated as completed reports; from `evidence_audit` onward the
413	present reports must be structurally valid. Structural validity is not proof
414	that acceptance criteria passed.
415	
416	### Gate binding (workflow_version 2)
417	
418	Recording the verdict with `set-gate` binds it to the audited bytes: State gains
419	`evidence.report_sha256` (SHA-256 of `evidence.md`) and `evidence.audit_sha256`
420	(SHA-256 of `evidence-audit.md`), and the Audit's Metadata `evidence_sha256` must
421	equal the current Evidence hash. The recorded `round` must name the Evidence
422	Metadata round. Changing either artifact after a sufficient verdict makes the
423	binding stale; `validate` and decisionward advances report the same blocker until
424	the auditor re-audits and re-runs `set-gate`. Version 1 Tickets keep the loose,
425	unbound gate.
426	
427	## Raw-byte transport (Git attributes)
428	
429	Every SHA-256 binding above hashes the artifact's **raw bytes** — line endings
430	included; bytes are never normalized before hashing. Git text normalization
431	(`core.autocrlf`, the `text` attribute) can rewrite those bytes on a fresh
432	clone or checkout and invalidate every binding, so transport is protected and
433	made visible:
434	
435	- `ai-workflow init` installs a single-purpose `.ai/work/.gitattributes`
436	  containing exactly `** -text` — but only when absent. An existing attribute
437	  file is never overwritten, and repeated init is byte-stable. The rule
438	  disables end-of-line conversion for everything under `.ai/work/`, so bound
439	  artifact bytes survive checkouts regardless of `autocrlf`.
440	- **Manual external-Plan rule:** a Plan outside `.ai/work/` is not covered by
441	  that file. Pin it with an explicit per-path `-text` rule in a root
442	  `.gitattributes` (e.g. `docs/plan.md -text`). Git attributes patterns split
443	  on whitespace, so a path containing a space cannot be written literally —
444	  use a glob instead (e.g. `docs/*.md -text`).
445	- `validate` and `resume` report a WARN-level transport notice for every bound
446	  artifact (sufficient-gate Evidence/audit bytes, a recorded Review artifact)
447	  and the registered Plan whose effective `text` attribute is anything other
448	  than unset — `text=auto`, `set`, or unspecified (autocrlf decides). The
449	  notice is visible only and never becomes a new execution gate; adding the
450	  `-text` rule is always the user's explicit decision. The assessment is
451	  read-only: it never edits root attributes or global config, and never
452	  renormalizes tracked files.
453	
454	Adopting protection for existing Tickets keeps their bindings: adding the
455	attributes file changes no committed artifact content, so current SHA-256
456	bindings stay current. Commit the attributes file itself and do **not**
457	renormalize (`git add --renormalize .` rewrites bytes and invalidates
458	bindings). Where Git attributes are unavailable — artifacts leaving the
459	repository by mail or attachment — a ZIP archive is the transport escape
460	hatch: an archive carries the bytes verbatim without attribute support.
461	
462	
463	## Verified export: `archive-artifacts` (manifest.json, format_version 1)
464	
465	`ai-workflow archive-artifacts <ticket-id> --output <new.zip>` publishes a
466	Ticket's work artifacts as a single ZIP of **exact raw bytes** plus a
467	`manifest.json` describing them. It is a verification boundary, not a generic
468	backup API: a v1 Ticket, a pending Review, or any stale binding is refused
469	(exit 1); both a `pass` and a *current* `changes_requested` verdict export.
470	
471	- **Export scope.** The archive collects the exact raw bytes of the State
472	  (`state.yaml`), Evidence, Evidence Audit, Decision, Progress, Handoff and
473	  Review artifacts, plus the registered Plan **at its actual registered source
474	  path** (from `source_artifacts.plan.path`), under safe unique
475	  repository-relative paths. Membership is fixed by this contract; the command
476	  takes no per-file options.
477	- **Currentness.** Before publication the collected bytes themselves are
478	  compared with every recorded hash — `evidence.report_sha256`,
479	  `evidence.audit_sha256`, `review.artifact_sha256`,
480	  `review.plan_sha256`/`source_artifacts.plan.sha256` — and the Review
481	  bindings are assessed WITHOUT the repair path's rework exception: a stale
482	  failed Review or an appended rework Plan awaiting a new review cannot be
483	  exported. Hashes are over raw bytes; line endings are never normalized.
484	- **Manifest.** `manifest.json` (JSON, `format_version: 1`) carries
485	  `ticket_id`, `snapshot_head` (the Git commit the export was taken at) and
486	  `entries`: a list sorted by repository-relative path, each entry holding
487	  `path`, `sha256` (of the member's raw bytes) and `bound_sha256` — the
488	  recorded State hash for the four bound members (Evidence, Audit, Review,
489	  registered Plan), and `null` for supporting files (`state.yaml`,
490	  `decision.md`, `progress.md`, `handoff.md`), which were never previously
491	  bound and are not pretended to be.
492	- **Safe publication.** Member names are validated before any write
493	  (normalized relative paths, no traversal, no duplicates; `manifest.json` is
494	  reserved), collected inputs must symlink-resolve inside the repository, and
495	  the output must not collide with a collected input or an existing file. The
496	  ZIP is built beside the output and published with a non-overwriting atomic
497	  hard link — `os.replace` is never used, so a pre-existing output keeps its
498	  exact bytes and a failed write leaves no partial archive. All failures are
499	  reported as errors; nothing is written on refusal.
500	- **Resuming elsewhere.** The archive re-verifies byte identity on arrival,
501	  but byte hashes alone do not re-establish the reviewed code: resume an
502	  exported Ticket WITH the matching code repository/history (the manifest's
503	  `snapshot_head` and `review.reviewed_commit` name the commits), or treat
504	  the archive as durable evidence only.
505
